verification_policy.identity_check: Confirm the artifact on the publisher's official domain or official repository.
verification_policy.content_check: Inspect the table, metadata, headers, units, and time coverage actually used by the normalizer.
verification_policy.second_check: Confirm the same scope in a separate publisher page, report note, metadata response, or independent authoritative series.
verification_policy.rule: A successful HTTP response alone is not evidence that a source supports a claim.

sources.title: Energy Data
sources.identity_check: Verified on the official OWID GitHub organization and repository documentation.
sources.content_check: The downloaded CSV contains World annual electricity-generation columns by fuel and technology through 2025; the normalizer retains the original column name in source_variable.
sources.second_check: IRENASTAT provides an official overlapping world series for renewable and non-renewable generation through 2023; it is retained separately because definitions and vintages differ.
sources.redistribution: Processed compilation with upstream-specific source and license requirements; retain attribution and consult the repository data catalog before publication.

sources.title: Monthly Energy Review Table 7.2a: Electricity Net Generation, Total (All Sectors)
sources.identity_check: Verified on EIA's official Monthly Energy Review data browser.
sources.content_check: Annual rows coded YYYY13 provide all-sector net generation by source in million kilowatthours from 1949 through 2025; the normalizer converts million kWh to TWh by multiplying by 0.001.
sources.second_check: EIA's Section 7 PDF table independently identifies the table as all-sector net generation, provides the same units, and defines the utility-scale solar scope.
sources.redistribution: U.S. federal statistical data; cite EIA and preserve table vintage and preliminary status.

sources.title: Monthly Energy Review Table 10.6: Solar Electricity Net Generation
sources.identity_check: Verified on EIA's official Monthly Energy Review data browser.
sources.content_check: Annual rows coded YYYY13 separately identify utility-scale, estimated small-scale, and total solar generation; the normalizer retains all three scopes.
sources.second_check: EIA's Section 10 PDF table independently documents the utility-scale and small-scale categories and units.
sources.redistribution: U.S. federal statistical data; cite EIA and retain estimate/preliminary labels.

sources.title: IRENASTAT Electricity Capacity by Region
sources.acquisition_method: PxWeb API POST selecting World, technologies, grid connection, and 2000-2025
sources.identity_check: Verified on IRENA's official PxWeb IRENASTAT host and download landing page.
sources.content_check: API metadata and returned CSV identify MW capacity, years 2000-2025, and explicit marine, geothermal, bioenergy, solar, wind, hydro, fossil, and nuclear categories.
sources.second_check: IRENA Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026 supplies overlapping official year-end capacity totals and definitions.
sources.redistribution: Retain IRENA attribution and check current IRENA data terms before public redistribution.

sources.title: IRENASTAT Electricity Generation by Region
sources.acquisition_method: PxWeb API POST selecting World, technologies, and 2000-2023
sources.identity_check: Verified on IRENA's official PxWeb IRENASTAT host and download landing page.
sources.content_check: API metadata and returned CSV identify GWh gross generation including self-consumption; 2024 was deliberately omitted because the publisher flags preliminary aggregate-generation quality concerns.
sources.second_check: The capacity table independently verifies technology names and provides a related but non-interchangeable measure.
sources.redistribution: Retain IRENA attribution and check current IRENA data terms before public redistribution.

sources.title: Annual Energy Outlook 2026 Reference and Side-Case Tables 8 and 16
sources.acquisition_method: HTTP GET of official XLSX workbooks for the baseline and ten side cases
sources.identity_check: Verified on EIA's official AEO2026 reference-table and side-case pages.
sources.content_check: The workbooks contain annual 2025-2050 generation and renewable-capacity series; internal EIA row codes, units, sectors, and case names are retained.
sources.second_check: EIA's table index describes Table 8 as electricity supply/generation and Table 16 as renewable energy by source; EIA methodology states AEO cases are projections under assumptions rather than predictions.
sources.redistribution: U.S. federal model output; cite EIA and label every series as scenario output.

sources.publisher: National Renewable Energy Laboratory, now National Laboratory of the Rockies
sources.title: 2024 Standard Scenarios Report: A U.S. Electricity Sector Outlook
sources.acquisition_method: Official Scenario Viewer project API; national annual CSV
sources.identity_check: Verified on the laboratory's official report, release page, and Scenario Viewer.
sources.content_check: The national file contains 61 ReEDS scenarios, nine modeled years from 2026 to 2050, and generation/capacity fields for fossil, CCS, nuclear, renewable, storage, and import technologies.
sources.second_check: The official report and laboratory release page independently describe the 61 scenarios, ReEDS model, contiguous-U.S. scope, and 2050 horizon.
sources.redistribution: Cite DOE, the laboratory, and Alliance for Sustainable Energy; retain the source disclaimer and scenario framing.

sources.publisher: Network for Greening the Financial System; hosted by IIASA
sources.title: NGFS Long-term Scenarios Phase 5.1
sources.acquisition_method: Official IIASA Scenario Explorer API metadata and bulk time-series query restricted to World electricity variables
sources.identity_check: Verified on the official NGFS data-resources portal and IIASA NGFS Scenario Explorer.
sources.content_check: The official API response supplies 21 model-scenario runs, three integrated-assessment models, seven scenarios, 53 electricity variables, and five-year values from 2020 through 2100 including 2050, 2060, and 2070.
sources.second_check: API model, scenario, unit, run, and time-series metadata endpoints were checked separately against the downloaded subset.
sources.redistribution: NGFS adapted-material terms require attribution and prohibit redistribution of a substantial portion of the database; only a narrow World-electricity subset is retained here.

sources.title: Scaling up investments in ocean energy technologies
sources.acquisition_method: Manual transcription of three explicitly labeled values from Figure 1; report is not redistributed
sources.identity_check: Verified on IRENA's official domain and publication PDF.
sources.content_check: Figure 1 gives global ocean-energy capacity of 0.535 GW in 2021, 70 GW in 2030, and 350 GW in 2050 under the cited WETO 2022 1.5-degree-C scenario.
sources.second_check: The surrounding report text separately states a 350 GW global market potential by 2050 and identifies wave and tidal stream as the most mature ocean technologies.
sources.redistribution: Only the three attributed figure values are stored; consult the report's current copyright notice for other reuse.
